newsitem.title: CHINA: ISLAND DYEING MULLS CHANGE OF CONTROL.
newsitem.headline: ISLAND DYEING MULLS CHANGE OF CONTROL.

text.p: Island Dyeing and Printing Co Ltd (IDP) said on Monday it was in talks with third parties on a possible asset injection that might lead to a change of control.

"The board continues to discuss with various independent third parties...with a view of either injecting assets into the company in exchange for new shares which might or might not result in a general offer being made," IDP said in a statement.
IDP said the third parties included parties believed to have a China background.

IDP said the third parties were also in talks with the company with a view to acquiring a controlling interest in IDP and/or acquiring an interest in the company's property located in Kwai Chung in Hong Kong's New Territories.
"Three parties are currently showing serious interest. So far no binding agreement has been concluded and discussions are still at a preliminary stage," IDP said.

Yu Ming Investments Ltd, formerly known as SHK Hong Kong Industries Ltd, said in a separate statement that it had been approached by independent third parties about buying part or all of its 33.71 percent stake in IDP.
"No decision has yet been made by the company as to whether it will dispose of its investment in IDP," it said.
Trading in IDP shares, suspended on August 7, and Yu Ming shares, suspended on August 8, is due to resume on Monday.
